vocational_public_structure.KVQ: The vocational/public structure names where contribution, visibility, credibility, and responsibility become part of the chart's ordinary architecture. When KVQ is the dominant EO current, that structure is filtered through the experience of noticing consequences, contradictions, or future implications before the room is ready to organize around them. This does not turn the public theme into a second report; it clarifies the bridge: your insight becomes most useful when it can be given timing, evidence, and language sturdy enough to hold up under scrutiny.
vocational_public_structure.MKI: This structural theme points to the public role as a place where work is not only performed, but carried forward. With MKI dominant, vocation may involve preserving knowledge, protecting continuity, or translating inherited material into a form other people can actually use. The natal layer describes the arena of responsibility; the EO layer adds the mythic texture of stewardship, showing where your contribution may become a living archive rather than a simple career path.
vocational_public_structure.RWI: The vocational/public structure shows where the chart asks for visible contribution, accountability, and a relationship to the larger world. When RWI leads the EO layer, that contribution is less about occupying a title and more about shaping the environment other people move through. The bridge is practical: your public life becomes a site of worldbuilding, where systems, stories, communities, or workflows reveal whether the vision can support real participation.
vocational_public_structure.DFIS: This natal structure describes the terms of visibility: what kind of role can be held, what authority is being negotiated, and where the public self meets expectation. With DFIS dominant, the EO layer brings sovereignty into that terrain. The bridge asks where public legitimacy has ever required self-abandonment, compliance, or silence, and where a more integrated form of power can be practiced without turning every appearance into a performance of permission.
vocational_public_structure.NGE: The vocational/public structure gives the chart a stage of consequence: work, reputation, contribution, and the roles through which others recognize you. When NGE is dominant, the EO layer frames that stage through narrative pattern rather than simple achievement. The useful question becomes not only what you are building, but what kind of story your public choices keep repeating, resolving, or refusing to outgrow.
vocational_public_structure.CATALYST: The vocational/public structure marks where your visible choices affect more than your private direction. With CATALYST dominant, the EO current emphasizes the way your role, work, or public presence can become a turning point in other people's timelines. This is not about making your vocation larger than life; it is about noticing where your accountability to your own path also changes the conditions, choices, or awakenings available around you.
vocational_public_structure.fallback: The vocational/public structure describes how contribution, recognition, responsibility, and long-term direction organize themselves in the chart. The EO layer does not replace that foundation; it adds a dominant symbolic current that colors how the person meets visibility and consequence. Read together, the bridge points to the kind of public role that can be inhabited without separating outer achievement from the deeper pattern moving through it.

relational_structure.KVQ: The relational structure shows how partnership, trust, reciprocity, and equal exchange are organized in the chart. When KVQ is dominant, that terrain is colored by the experience of sensing subtext before it has been said plainly. The bridge is not suspicion; it is translation. Relational clarity strengthens when early perception is given clean language, observable context, and enough patience for the other person to meet the truth without being forced into it.
relational_structure.MKI: This structural theme describes the agreements, attachments, and relational patterns that shape how a person meets others as equals. With MKI dominant, relationship is also a vessel for memory: family stories, inherited expectations, old loyalties, and forms of wisdom carried through connection. The natal layer names the relational arena; the EO layer shows where bonds may ask for continuity, repair, or a more conscious relationship to what has been passed down.
relational_structure.RWI: Relational structure is where the chart describes partnership as an actual system: the agreements people repeat, the roles they occupy, and the shared world their choices create. When RWI leads the EO layer, connection becomes a site of worldbuilding rather than simple compatibility. The bridge asks what kind of relational environment is being woven through habits, language, repair, conflict, pleasure, and the practical terms of living life beside another person.
relational_structure.DFIS: This natal structure points to the conditions under which closeness, equality, and commitment can function without distortion. With DFIS dominant, the EO layer brings the question of sovereignty directly into relationship. The bridge is especially clear where love, loyalty, desire, or belonging has ever been confused with surrendering authority over the self. Connection becomes healthier when devotion and autonomy are allowed to stand in the same room.
relational_structure.NGE: The relational structure describes how the chart organizes partnership, projection, attraction, conflict, and mutual recognition. When NGE is dominant, the EO layer reads that terrain through narrative pattern: the roles people are invited to play, the story a bond keeps rehearsing, and the moment when a familiar script needs a different ending. The bridge is not about romanticizing relationship; it is about noticing which stories create real reciprocity and which only create momentum.
relational_structure.CATALYST: This structural theme names the relationships that alter direction, reveal contrast, and draw hidden choices into the open. With CATALYST dominant, the EO layer emphasizes the way encounter itself can become a turning point. The bridge does not make one person responsible for another person's transformation; it shows where relational contact can wake up a choice, expose a pattern, or move both people closer to a truth neither could reach alone.
relational_structure.fallback: The relational structure describes how partnership, reciprocity, conflict, projection, and mutual recognition take shape in the natal chart. The EO layer does not replace that architecture; it adds the dominant current moving through the person's way of meeting others. Read together, the bridge points to the kind of connection that can hold both ordinary relational skill and the deeper symbolic pattern that keeps appearing through relationship.

inner_life_restoration_structure.KVQ: The inner life/restoration structure describes the chart's architecture for privacy, recovery, regulation, and the material that needs time away from performance. When KVQ is dominant, that inward terrain is shaped by the cost of sensing what was real before it could be confirmed, named, or welcomed by others. The bridge asks for a gentler kind of discernment: not every early signal has to become an alarm, but the body still deserves a place where its perceptions can be sorted, grounded, and believed.
inner_life_restoration_structure.MKI: This structural theme points to the private places where memory lives: the family archive, the body, the dream life, the ancestral pattern, and the habits that were inherited before they were chosen. With MKI dominant, restoration often comes through recovering context rather than trying to erase the past. The natal layer names the need for inner repair; the EO layer shows where old knowledge, old grief, or old protection can be brought into the present with more consciousness and less repetition.
inner_life_restoration_structure.RWI: Inner restoration is not only rest; it is the private architecture that makes a life inhabitable. When RWI leads the EO layer, the bridge turns inward toward the systems, rituals, stories, and environments that shape emotional weather before anyone else sees the result. The chart describes where recovery is needed; the EO current shows how a more livable inner world can be woven through small repeated choices, not only through major breakthroughs.
inner_life_restoration_structure.DFIS: The inner life/restoration structure names the places where the self meets silence, shame, instinct, exhaustion, and the unfinished emotional material that cannot be solved by performing wellness. With DFIS dominant, the EO layer brings sovereignty into the hidden room. The bridge asks where healing has ever been confused with becoming easier to tolerate, and where restoration now means returning authority to the body, the boundary, the desire, or the truth that was pushed underground.
inner_life_restoration_structure.NGE: This natal structure describes the private plotline: what the person returns to when the public story quiets, which old roles still organize the nervous system, and what kind of rest allows a different chapter to become possible. When NGE is dominant, the EO layer reads restoration through narrative pattern without forcing everything into a dramatic climax. The bridge is the recognition that an inner story can change first in tone, pacing, and self-witnessing before it changes in outward events.
inner_life_restoration_structure.CATALYST: Inner restoration shows where experience has to be metabolized before it can become wisdom. With CATALYST dominant, the EO layer emphasizes the private aftermath of turning points: the encounter, rupture, awakening, or sudden recognition that keeps moving through the body after the moment itself has passed. The bridge does not ask the person to become endlessly available for transformation; it shows where integration requires privacy, softness, and enough space for the nervous system to catch up with what the soul already knows.
inner_life_restoration_structure.fallback: The inner life/restoration structure describes how the natal chart organizes privacy, recovery, emotional regulation, unconscious patterning, and the quiet work of becoming whole enough to participate again. The EO layer does not replace that foundation; it adds the dominant symbolic current moving through the person's restoration process. Read together, the bridge points to the kind of healing that can honor both the chart's private architecture and the deeper current asking to be integrated there.
